description: Search all pattern occurrences by streaming through the pattern suffix automaton and following suffix links.

source.title: Forward Dawg Matching algorithm
source.book_reference: Maxime Crochemore and Wojciech Rytter, Text Algorithms, Oxford University Press, 1994
source.source_license: Copyright belongs to cited authors and publishers. Mathematical descriptions only; independent implementation and workload.

workspace.meaning: Pattern staging, a dense 258-state by four-symbol transition table, suffix links, maximum state lengths, and bounded local state. The text is read directly from the validated input frame.

contract.automaton: Build the minimal suffix automaton of the pattern by the standard online extension algorithm; absent transitions are -1 and suffix links are followed to the first state with a transition.
contract.streaming_state: Scan text left-to-right. Track the automaton state and the length of the longest pattern factor ending at the current text position; on a suffix-link fallback with a transition, set the length to max_length[fallback_state]+1.
contract.occurrences: Report start j-pattern_length+1 whenever the matched-factor length equals pattern_length; continue scanning so overlapping occurrences are included.
contract.complexity: O(m) preprocessing and O(n) search for the fixed four-symbol alphabet; the published algorithm inspects exactly n text symbols.
contract.state_bound: At most 2*m states for m>=1; the allocated bound is 2*128+2=258 states.
contract.workspace_bound: 6*258*8 + 128*8 + bounded scalar storage is below 16384 bytes; clone rows are copied directly into the transition table.
contract.result_bounds: At most 4096 matches and the sum of offsets is below 2^23, so the packed result is below 2^49 and fits signed 64-bit.
contract.error_precedence: Validate the input pointer, parseable length, header, exact packed length, and symbol ranges before automaton construction.
